cases.name: cuts on punctuation and holds through an abbreviation

input.text: Alpha beta gamma delta, epsilon zeta eta theta. Dr. Seward came quickly, then opened the door.

cases.note: "Dr." is an abbreviation, so its period does not cut; the four phrases are four words each.

cases.name: merges a short opening fragment forward

input.text: One, two three four five.

cases.note: A one-word opening fragment is below the four-word minimum, so it joins the phrase after it.

cases.name: cuts a real French paragraph as French

input.text: Longtemps, je me suis couché de bonne heure. Parfois, à peine ma bougie éteinte, mes yeux se fermaient si vite que je n’avais pas le temps de me dire : « Je m’endors. »

cases.name: cuts the same French paragraph as English

input.text: Longtemps, je me suis couché de bonne heure. Parfois, à peine ma bougie éteinte, mes yeux se fermaient si vite que je n’avais pas le temps de me dire : « Je m’endors. »

cases.note: The two cuts of this paragraph differ by exactly one word from the second phrase on: "à" counts as a word under the French fold and vanishes under the English delete, and every later phrase inherits the offset.

cases.name: folds a French book's accents into the alphabet

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.note: il · etait · une · fois · a · paris ‖ un · homme · tres · age

cases.name: folds the typographic apostrophe and the ligatures

input.text: L’esprit du cœur, et l’âme naïve, æther.

cases.note: l'esprit · du · coeur · et · l'ame · naive · aether — the typographic apostrophe is the apostrophe, and œ/æ spell themselves out.

cases.name: guillemets and a bare exclamation are not words

input.text: « Bonjour ! » dit-elle à l’enfant, très doucement, puis elle sortit.

cases.note: bonjour · ditelle · a · l'enfant · tres · doucement · puis · elle · sortit

cases.name: a French title does not cut the phrase in half

input.text: Mme. Dupont arriva; Mlle. Leroy la suivait de près.

cases.note: "Mlle." is a French abbreviation, so the whole line is one phrase: mme · dupont · arriva · mlle · leroy · la · suivait · de · pres

cases.name: a region-tagged language reduces to its primary subtag

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.name: a language tag is matched case-insensitively

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.name: an unlisted language folds

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.name: an unlisted language keeps the English abbreviations

input.text: Mme. Dupont arriva; Mlle. Leroy la suivait de près.

cases.note: Folding is what the acoustics need; a missing abbreviation costs one extra phrase boundary, a missing fold costs the word itself.

cases.name: English deletes rather than folds

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.note: "à" is not a word to the English rule at all; "très" is "trs" and "âgé" is "g".

cases.name: English is the default when no language is given

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.name: a French title is not an English abbreviation

input.text: Mme. Dupont arriva; Mlle. Leroy la suivait de près.

cases.name: English drops the typographic apostrophe

input.text: « Bonjour ! » dit-elle à l’enfant, très doucement, puis elle sortit.

cases.note: The apostrophe is deleted rather than folded, so l’enfant becomes "lenfant" — one word, where French reads two.

cases.name: an English book saying à la carte counts nine words

input.text: A la carte à la carte naïve café stands here.

cases.name: the same line read as French counts ten

input.text: A la carte à la carte naïve café stands here.

cases.name: an empty language tag is read as English

input.text: Il était une fois, à Paris, un homme très âgé.

cases.note: Extra case: an empty tag neither folds nor selects a language-specific abbreviation set, so it behaves exactly as English.

cases.name: a short fragment joins the phrase before it

input.text: Alpha beta gamma delta, oh my, epsilon zeta eta theta.

cases.note: Extra case: the two-word fragment between the commas is below the minimum, so it is appended to the phrase before it rather than standing alone.

cases.name: a single-letter initial does not cut, a comma always does

input.text: Mr. H. Rider Haggard wrote it, and then he left. The night was very long indeed.

cases.note: Extra case: "Mr." is an abbreviation and "H." has a single-letter core, so neither period cuts; the comma after "it" cuts regardless, because the abbreviation guard covers only . ? ! and ;.

cases.name: whitespace-only text is one empty phrase
cases.note: Extra case: nothing tokenizes, so the fallback single phrase holds no words and its cumulative end is 0.

cases.name: an accented single letter is not a word by default
an accented single letter is not an English word
an accented single letter is a French word
a ligature word survives the French fold
a ligature word survives the English strip
cases.note: English deletes the ligature rather than spelling it out, leaving "uvre" — still a word, just a different one.

cases.name: a guillemet is not a word
an em dash is not a word
a number is not a word
cases.note: Extra case: digits are outside the alphabet in every language, so nothing survives.
